definition: what the colours on a stoplight bar of mine are pinned to, and why they move

settled:
A stoplight of mine is pinned partly to my own distribution rather than wholly to anything absolute.

Four bands, not three, and green is my median rather than my middle band. Green is the median and everything above it, which is where I have been living. Yellow at one sigma down is caution. Red at two sigma down is alarm. Black at three or four sigma down is crisis.

The anchoring is a deliberate mix of absolute and relative. What I tune it for is differentiation, so the scale keeps telling me something rather than parking me in one band for months.

It moves slowly, on a lot of evidence rather than on recent readings. Recovery raising my baseline recalibrates it.

The case put to me was that a turbulent stretch widens my spread and pushes the alarm bands further down in absolute terms exactly as life gets harder. I granted having seen it happen before and did not treat it as disqualifying. I keep them where they are, because communicating the actual state is the right thing.
